title: Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner
goal:
Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Survey answers (if any) live in docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE_SURVEY.md. Section: RESPONSE.md S4, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md, WIDE_NET Cause 4. Survey: q5 (survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal).

Evidence: "501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502 since 11-19 on server2-alpha; a proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20-20:40:57 during backend build 637. Today any in-try backend-call failure inside executeAssignment sends an interrupt and rethrows -> process exit -> systemd restart. Heartbeat failures are tolerated (lease TTL) but in-assignment call failures are fatal, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run."

MUST-READ BEFORE CODING: docs/tasks/db49d6c6-*/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (runner recovery containment) - build on it or explicitly scope against it; do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure.

Change (runner, runner/daemon.js + runner/client.js): (1) executeAssignment catch (runner/daemon.js:2299-2452): transient backend errors (fetch failed network errors, 502/503/504) during an assignment send interrupt WITH reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing - same report-and-return precedent as WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED and deterministic-gitFailure branches. (2) bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (heartbeat, dispatch poll) so idle loop stops crash-cycling (restart counters 366->367 in 11-19 sample) - or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit. (3) keep FATAL: STALE_EPOCH, auth failures, genuinely unknown errors - enumerate the non-fatal set explicitly, never invert the catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.

Tests: runner/client.backendOutage.test.js (GUIDE-04 section 2: 502 shape, dropped-socket shape, recovery) + section 3 fatality-boundary test flipped red (expect(rethrown).toBe(false) transient, still-true stale-epoch). Register in scripts/run-tests.mjs. Confirm: E4 timestamp-join on db24c124, 1f8959ca, f56e9878, ef21e99b, bae668cb (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission); after rollout, crash-restart rate in runner journal drops while assignment success holds.

# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment

Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).

## Goal

1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.

## Success Criteria

- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.

## Survey decisions (factored in)

`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):

| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |

## Approach

Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":

1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.

No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.

## Evidence (what the research established)

- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.
- **Crash path:** `executeAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2243–2333) catches generic errors, best-effort `client.interrupt`s, then **rethrows** (line 2332). `runDispatchLoop` awaits `executeAssignment` (line 2928) with **no `try/catch`**, and the loop body has only `try/finally` — so the throw escapes `runLoop` → `main()` (`runner/main.js`) rejects → process exits 1 → systemd restarts → the interrupted task re-queues and the same poisoned worktree is reclaimed → observed 10,776-restart loop. The `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` precedent (interrupt + return, lines 2246–2262) shows the codebase's own pattern for "infra problem, don't die".
- **Hook mechanics:** `scripts/githooks/pre-commit` is the binary guard; `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks` is set repo-wide and inherited by linked `kb-*` worktrees (existing test at `runner/project.test.js` ~line 364 proves inheritance). So a corrupt PNG staged anywhere in a reused/evicted worktree deterministically aborts both recovery commits today.
- **Test patterns to reuse:** `originWithWorktree()` + `refreshWorktreeToRemote` reuse test (~line 73), eviction parking test (~line 525), staged-index regression test (~line 731), `localRepo()` helper (~line 27). New tests mirror these with a failing hook installed.
- **Test entrypoints:** focused — `node --test runner/project.test.js`; full unit gate — `npm test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, "Unit Tests (runner)" suite names `runner/*.test.js` explicitly).

## Key Decisions

1. **Scope of `--no-verify`: recovery snapshots only (survey q1).** These commits are local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*`, never pushed as task output and never merged; hook value there is zero and hook cost is a wedged runner. All other runner-authored commits keep hooks. Rejected: `--no-verify` everywhere (loses the binary-guard backstop on real output), and deleting/disabling repo hooks (mutates user repos).
2. **Containment via loop-level catch, keeping `interrupt` routing (survey q2, refined).** The minimal correct fix is `try/catch` around `await executeAssignment(...)` in `runDispatchLoop`: log the error, continue polling. The task is already released by the `interrupt` inside `executeAssignment`'s catch, satisfying "failing/releasing the task cleanly". Changing generic errors to `complete(outcome: failed)` instead would newly fail tasks for transient infra blips (network, lock contention) — a behavior change far beyond this task — so routing is left untouched. Rejected: removing the rethrow in `executeAssignment` (breaks `runSingleAssignment`'s non-zero-exit contract and the `STALE_EPOCH` contract).
3. **Shared helper over two one-line edits.** Both commit blocks duplicate identity flags and message shape; a `commitRecoverySnapshot(workdir, message, { logger })` helper (name to match repo conventions at implementation time) makes the bypass auditable in one place and prevents future drift between the paths. The helper owns: `-c` identity flags, `--no-verify`, the message, and the q3 warn log.
4. **Failing-hook fixture, not the real binary guard, in tests.** Tests install a trivial `#!/bin/sh; exit 1` hook (via `core.hooksPath` on a fixture dir or a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file in the temp repo) so they are hermetic, fast, and independent of `check-binary-guard.mjs` internals. One test may additionally exercise the real guard with a corrupt PNG if cheap, but it is not required.

## Steps

### Step 0 — Recon and reproduce (research; no behavior change)

- Confirm the two commit sites and the `runDispatchLoop` → `executeAssignment` → `prepareWorkdir` → `runGit` throw chain on the current checkout (line numbers above were read this session; re-verify at implementation time).
- Run the existing recovery tests green as a baseline: `node --test runner/project.test.js`.

Read text file `docs/tasks/db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment
2|
3|Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
4|Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
5|Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).
6|
7|## Goal
8|
9|1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
10|2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
11|3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.
12|
13|## Success Criteria
14|
15|- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
16|- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
17|- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
18|- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.
19|
20|## Survey decisions (factored in)
21|
22|`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):
23|
24|| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
25||---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
26|| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
27|| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
28|| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |
29|
30|## Approach
31|
32|Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":
33|
34|1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
35|2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
36|3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.
37|
38|No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.
39|
40|## Evidence (what the research established)
41|
42|- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.

1|# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment
2|
3|Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
4|Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
5|Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).
6|
7|## Goal
8|
9|1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
10|2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
11|3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.
12|
13|## Success Criteria
14|
15|- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
16|- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
17|- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
18|- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.
19|
20|## Survey decisions (factored in)
21|
22|`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):
23|
24|| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
25||---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
26|| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
27|| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
28|| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |
29|
30|## Approach
31|
32|Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":
33|
34|1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
35|2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
36|3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.
37|
38|No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.
39|
40|## Evidence (what the research established)
41|
42|- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.
43|- **Crash path:** `executeAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2243–2333) catches generic errors, best-effort `client.interrupt`s, then **rethrows** (line 2332). `runDispatchLoop` awaits `executeAssignment` (line 2928) with **no `try/catch`**, and the loop body has only `try/finally` — so the throw escapes `runLoop` → `main()` (`runner/main.js`) rejects → process exits 1 → systemd restarts → the interrupted task re-queues and the same poisoned worktree is reclaimed → observed 10,776-restart loop. The `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` precedent (interrupt + return, lines 2246–2262) shows the codebase's own pattern for "infra problem, don't die".
44|- **Hook mechanics:** `scripts/githooks/pre-commit` is the binary guard; `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks` is set repo-wide and inherited by linked `kb-*` worktrees (existing test at `runner/project.test.js` ~line 364 proves inheritance). So a corrupt PNG staged anywhere in a reused/evicted worktree deterministically aborts both recovery commits today.
45|- **Test patterns to reuse:** `originWithWorktree()` + `refreshWorktreeToRemote` reuse test (~line 73), eviction parking test (~line 525), staged-index regression test (~line 731), `localRepo()` helper (~line 27). New tests mirror these with a failing hook installed.
46|- **Test entrypoints:** focused — `node --test runner/project.test.js`; full unit gate — `npm test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, "Unit Tests (runner)" suite names `runner/*.test.js` explicitly).
47|
48|## Key Decisions
49|
50|1. **Scope of `--no-verify`: recovery snapshots only (survey q1).** These commits are local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*`, never pushed as task output and never merged; hook value there is zero and hook cost is a wedged runner. All other runner-authored commits keep hooks. Rejected: `--no-verify` everywhere (loses the binary-guard backstop on real output), and deleting/disabling repo hooks (mutates user repos).
51|2. **Containment via loop-level catch, keeping `interrupt` routing (survey q2, refined).** The minimal correct fix is `try/catch` around `await executeAssignment(...)` in `runDispatchLoop`: log the error, continue polling. The task is already released by the `interrupt` inside `executeAssignment`'s catch, satisfying "failing/releasing the task cleanly". Changing generic errors to `complete(outcome: failed)` instead would newly fail tasks for transient infra blips (network, lock contention) — a behavior change far beyond this task — so routing is left untouched. Rejected: removing the rethrow in `executeAssignment` (breaks `runSingleAssignment`'s non-zero-exit contract and the `STALE_EPOCH` contract).
52|3. **Shared helper over two one-line edits.** Both commit blocks duplicate identity flags and message shape; a `commitRecoverySnapshot(workdir, message, { logger })` helper (name to match repo conventions at implementation time) makes the bypass auditable in one place and prevents future drift between the paths. The helper owns: `-c` identity flags, `--no-verify`, the message, and the q3 warn log.
53|4. **Failing-hook fixture, not the real binary guard, in tests.** Tests install a trivial `#!/bin/sh; exit 1` hook (via `core.hooksPath` on a fixture dir or a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file in the temp repo) so they are hermetic, fast, and independent of `check-binary-guard.mjs` internals. One test may additionally exercise the real guard with a corrupt PNG if cheap, but it is not required.
54|

62|- Depends on: nothing. Validates: problem statement is still accurate.

64|### Step 1 — Make the change easy: extract helper + fixture (refactor; no behavior change)

No `--no-verify` yet. Update the MARK/JSDoc comments on `preserveEvictedWorkdir` / `refreshWorktreeToRemote` to point at the helper.
67|- In `runner/project.test.js`, add a `installFailingHook(repoDir)` fixture helper (writes an always-fail `pre-commit`, wires it via `core.hooksPath` or `.git/hooks`, asserts it actually fires with a scratch commit).
68|- Depends on: Step 0. Validates: `node --test runner/project.test.js` green; `git diff` shows argv-identical behavior (review the two call sites).
69|
70|### Step 2 — Make the change: `--no-verify` + warn log + regression tests
71|
72|- Add `--no-verify` to the helper's commit argv and a warn-level log naming the recovery branch/message and stating hooks were bypassed (survey q3). Thread the logger through (check how `project.js` logs today; if it has no logger, `console.warn` via an injectable param defaulting to console, matching testability).
73|- Add two regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` (mirror existing patterns):
74|  1. **Reuse:** `originWithWorktree()`-style setup + failing hook + dirty file → `refreshWorktreeToRemote` resolves, `recoveredTo` matches `^kb-recovery/…`, parked file present via `git ls-tree`, worktree clean.
75|  2. **Eviction:** `localRepo()` + `prepareWorkdir` + failing hook + dirty/staged file → `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (and/or the cap-eviction flow from the ~line 525 test) resolves, `kb-recovery/…` branch exists with the file, task-branch tip unchanged (mirror the ~line 731 assertions).
76|- Prove red→green: run the new tests against the pre-Step-2 helper (stash the argv change) to confirm they fail, then with the change to confirm they pass.
77|- Depends on: Step 1. Validates: new tests fail-before / pass-after; full `node --test runner/project.test.js` green.

79|### Step 3 — Daemon containment: per-task catch in the dispatch loop
80|
81|- Wrap the `await executeAssignment({...})` call in `runDispatchLoop` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2928) in `try/catch`: on error, `logger.error`/`logger.warn` with task/project IDs and the message, then continue polling. Keep the post-assignment reap + self-update flow reachable after a caught error (place the catch so the loop proceeds to the next iteration cleanly; decide at implementation time whether reap should run for the failed assignment — recommended: yes, keep it inline by catching narrowly around `executeAssignment` only).
82|- Audit (no change expected, verify by reading): `runSingleAssignment` keeps throw/exit-non-zero; `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (it must — epoch fencing); `executeIntegrationAssignment` throws are also covered by the same loop catch; `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` path unchanged.
83|- Add a `runner/daemon.test.js` test: stub `prepareWorkdir` (or the client/claim seam the existing daemon tests use) to throw on the first assignment and succeed/stop on the second poll; assert the loop survives the first failure and processes the second (or exits its bounded test run) instead of rejecting. Follow existing `daemon.test.js` fakes — do not build a new harness double if one exists.
84|- Depends on: Step 2 (independent code-wise, but sequenced after so the primary fix lands first). Validates: new daemon test fails-before (loop rejects) / passes-after; `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` green.
85|
86|### Step 4 — Docs, hygiene, and full gates
87|
88|- Update `runner/README.md` recovery/eviction section if it describes recovery commits or loop failure handling (short note: recovery snapshots bypass hooks by design; dispatch loop isolates per-task failures). Keep JSDoc on touched functions accurate.
89|- Run the full gates: `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js`, then `npm test` (root, covers the runner suite) and any lint gate the repo configures for `runner/` (check `package.json` scripts / CI at implementation time).
90|- Re-verify non-goals: `git commit` argv for wrap-up/integration commits untouched; no hook files in the repo modified.
91|- Depends on: Steps 2–3.
92|
93|## Validation Plan
94|
95|| Check | Command / evidence | Expected |
96||-------|--------------------|----------|
97|| Focused recovery tests | `node --test runner/project.test.js` | All pass, incl. 2 new failing-hook tests |
98|| Focused daemon tests | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` | All pass, incl. new loop-survival test |
99|| Red→green proof | New tests vs pre-fix helper (Step 2) and pre-fix loop (Step 3) | Fail before, pass after (record output in the task docs) |
100|| Full unit gate | `npm test` | Green (runner suite included via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) |
101|| Manual repro | `/tmp` script from Step 0 re-run post-fix | Both paths park cleanly with failing hook |
102|| Scope audit | `git diff --stat` + grep `--no-verify` in `runner/` | Only the helper + tests + loop catch + docs touched |
103|
104|Highest-risk validation: the Step 3 daemon test — `runDispatchLoop` is timing/poll-driven, so the test must bound the loop deterministically using existing test seams; if no clean seam exists, prefer extracting a tiny `runOneDispatchIteration` pure-ish unit over sleeping/flaky polling.
105|
106|## Risks
107|
108|- **Masking real damage (q1 trade-off):** bypassed snapshots can park corrupt binaries. Accepted by design (survey q1): recovery branches are forensic snapshots, and the q3 warn log preserves discoverability. Mitigation: log message includes branch name + reason.
109|- **Poison-task flap:** after containment, a task whose setup fails persistently will interrupt/re-queue and be reclaimed repeatedly (runner survives, task flaps). This matches the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` behavior and is strictly better than a restart storm; consecutive-failure backoff is explicitly out of scope (see Non-goals).
110|- **Logger threading in `project.js`:** if the module currently never logs, adding a logger param touches several signatures. Mitigation: optional param defaulting to console; keep the diff minimal.
111|
112|## Non-goals
113|
114|- Changing `interrupt` → `complete(failed)` routing for generic errors.
115|- Consecutive-failure backoff/circuit-breaking for flapping tasks.
116|- `--no-verify` on any non-recovery commit (wrap-up, integration merge, stage output).
117|- Touching `scripts/githooks/*`, hook installation, or the binary guard itself.
118|- Systemd unit changes (no `Restart=` tuning needed once the process stops crashing).
119|
120|## Open Questions
121|
122|1. **Survey confirmation:** `SURVEY.md` answers are empty — confirm the three adopted recommended options (q1 emergency-only bypass, q2 fail/move-on refined to interrupt-and-continue, q3 warn log). If q2's literal "mark failed" is required instead of interrupt-and-continue, Step 3 needs a routing change with wider blast radius — decide before implementing Step 3. (Default if unanswered: proceed as planned.)
123|2. None other — all technical facts were verified in-repo this session.
124|

126|
127|Big/research pieces first per the stage brief: Step 0 (repro + chain verification) and the Step 3 seam investigation are the riskiest and come before/around the small behavior edits. Steps 1–2 are small and mechanical once the helper shape is chosen. {"content":"# Implementation Plan — In-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4)

Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`
Source problem: any in-try backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and rethrows → process exit → systemd restart, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run (501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502s since 11-19 on server2-alpha; proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).
Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1, q1–q4; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).

## Goal

1. Transient backend errors (fetch-failed network errors, HTTP 502/503/504) raised during an assignment make `executeAssignment` send an interrupt WITH a reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing — the same report-and-return precedent as the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and deterministic-gitFailure branches.
2. The idle loop stops crash-cycling on backend outages: bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (dispatch poll; heartbeat already warn-continues), or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit.
3. The non-fatal set is enumerated explicitly; `STALE_EPOCH`, auth failures, and genuinely unknown errors stay fatal. No inverted catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.
4. Regression tests in `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (+ daemon fatality-boundary tests) prove the transient/fatal boundary, registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.

## Success Criteria

- A 502/503/504 or dropped-socket failure from any backend call inside `executeAssignment` produces a best-effort `interrupt` carrying a reason, a one-line log naming the cause, and a return (no throw) — the dispatch loop keeps polling and the process stays alive.
- A dispatch-poll (`dispatchClaim`) transient failure backs off and re-polls without consuming idle budget and without exiting; restart counters stop incrementing across a backend restart window.
- `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (epoch fencing intact), auth/credential failures still exit loud, and unknown errors still throw — proven by boundary tests asserting `rethrown === false` for transient and `rethrown === true` for stale-epoch.
- `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js runner/daemon.test.js runner/client.test.js` passes, the repo unit gate (`npm test` via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes, and the new suite file is registered (the `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pin fails the gate if it is not).
- Post-rollout (needs PROD-READ-ONLY permission): crash-restart rate in the runner journal drops across backend restart windows while assignment success holds; E4 timestamp-join confirmed on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`.

## Survey decisions (factored in)

Local `SURVEY.md` Round 1 is unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions). The stage brief also cites the source-task survey q5 ("survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal") — that maps to local q2 and is adopted the same way.

| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
| q1 | Mid-task connection drop: what should the worker do? | Stay alive, report what happened, keep checking for work | Interrupt-with-reason + return; never rethrow for the transient set. |
| q2 (= source q5) | Which problems to survive vs still stop for? | Only survive short connection problems (network errors, 502/503/504); still stop for login problems, outdated orders, anything unknown | Explicit non-fatal enumeration (`isTransientBackendError`); `STALE_EPOCH`/auth/unknown stay fatal. |
| q3 | Idle poll/heartbeat outage: what to do? | Retry a few times with growing waits, then keep waiting without restarting | Bounded retries with backoff on idempotent idle calls; minimum acceptable fallback is sleep-and-continue. |
| q4 (optional) | Log visibility for ride-through? | A clear one-line note naming the cause, then keep going | One `warn`/`error` line with cause + task/project IDs per ride-through; no per-retry spam (retry attempts at debug/quiet). |

## Approach

Follow "make the change easy, then make the change", and build on the db49d6c6 containment — do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure:

1. **Easy first:** extract one shared `isTransientBackendError(err)` classifier (single home for the explicit non-fatal set) plus shared test fixtures (502-shape stub, dropped-socket stub), with zero behavior change. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
2. **Then the change:** add one narrow branch in the `executeAssignment` catch using the classifier (interrupt-with-reason + return), mirroring the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape; same one-branch treatment for the `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (parity, decided in Key Decision 4).
3. **Then the idle loop:** transient-aware handling in the `dispatchClaim` catch (backoff + re-poll, no idle-budget consumption); verify the heartbeat timer path already tolerates outages (it warns-and-continues today) and add bounded join-time retries only if the Step 0 probe shows join is a live crash path.
4. **Then proof:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + daemon boundary tests, registration in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, red→green runs, full gates, rollout/confirm plan.

No new dependencies, no new config flags (backoff constants are module-local), no schema/wire changes (the interrupt `reason` field already exists).

## Evidence (what the research established)

Verified in-repo this session (line numbers are the current checkout — re-verify at implementation time):

- **In-assignment catch:** `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js` ~2296–2453) special-cases `STALE_EPOCH` (rethrow, line 2298), `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (interrupt-with-reason + return, lines 2299–2315), deterministic gitFailure (report + return, lines 2316–2376), `failedOutcome` (failed completion, lines 2377–2428), then the generic path: flush, best-effort interrupt with reason, **`throw err`** (lines 2441–2452). The S4 branch slots in just before the generic path, copying the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape.
- **db49d6c6 containment already landed (build on it):** `runDispatchLoop` wraps `executeAssignment` in try/catch (~3097–3153): `STALE_EPOCH` rethrows, anything else is logged and contained. So in dispatch mode a rethrow no longer exits — but the stage brief's crash path is still live in three places: (a) `dispatchClaim` unknown errors `throw err` at line 3018 → loop exits → systemd restart (this is the 366→367 crash-cycling); (b) `runSingleAssignment` has no loop, so any rethrow exits non-zero; (c) `joinAndHeartbeat` failures before the loop starts exit the process. S4 must target exactly these, not rework the db49 catch.
- **Client error shapes** (`runner/client.js` `call`, lines 17–40): non-2xx throws `Error` with `statusCode = res.status` and `code = data?.code ?? null` — so a 502 arrives as `{ statusCode: 502, code }`. A dropped socket / refused connection rejects `fetchImpl` itself (raw `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET` causes) with no `statusCode`. The classifier must cover both shapes.
- **Heartbeat already tolerates outages:** the periodic timer (`deliverSteers(...).catch(warn)`, lines 1241–1245) and claim renewal (`claimHeartbeat(...).then(warn)`, lines 796–808) both warn-and-continue; heartbeat failures ride the lease TTL. The idle-loop crash-cycling is the dispatch-poll path, not the heartbeat path.
- **Integration parity site:** `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (~2655–2697) ends in the same interrupt + `throw err` (lines 2687–2696).
- **Fatality contract pinned by an existing test:** `runner/daemon.test.js` "never idles out with dispatchIdleLimit 0" throws a generic `persistent-loop-probe` error from `dispatchClaim` and asserts the loop rejects — unknown dispatch errors MUST keep throwing after S4 (consistent with q2). S4's dispatch branch must only catch the classifier-positive set.
- **Test seams to reuse:** `stubClient` / `fakeHarness` / `localRepo` / `loopConfig` helpers and the `waitFor` polling helper in `runner/daemon.test.js`; `stubFetch` + `ok`/`fail` helpers in `runner/client.test.js`.
- **Test registration:** `scripts/run-tests.mjs` "Unit Tests (runner)" (~lines 460–491) names every `runner/*.test.js` explicitly, and `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every suite file on disk is registered — a new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` must be added to that list or the gate fails.
- **Evidence gap (does not block):** the cited source-research folder `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/` (`RESPONSE.md` S4, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 4, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q5) is absent from this checkout (verified: no such folder; repo-wide search for `backend-unreachable|WIDE_NET|Backend 502` finds nothing). The GUIDE-04 §2/§3 test shapes are therefore reconstructed from the stage brief plus the in-repo client shapes above; Step 0 re-derives the exact 502/dropped-socket fixtures from `runner/client.js` and Node fetch behavior rather than trusting the brief's prose. If the folder exists upstream, pull it in Step 0 and reconcile (shapes should match; any conflict is resolved in favor of the observed client behavior).

## Key Decisions

1. **Explicit non-fatal enumeration, never an inverted catch-all (survey q2).** One `isTransientBackendError(err)` predicate owns the set: `statusCode ∈ {502, 503, 504}` OR a network-layer failure (fetch rejection: `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`/`EAI_AGAIN`/socket-hangup causes — exact list fixed in Step 0 from observed shapes). Everything else falls through to today's generic path. New failure modes stay loud by construction.
2. **Classifier lives next to the client, used by the daemon.** Recommended: export from `runner/client.js` (it defines the error shapes) and import in `runner/daemon.js`. Rejected: duplicating status checks at each catch site (drifts), or putting it in `shared/` (runner-only concern; no backend/wire change).
3. **In-assignment branch = interrupt-with-reason + return, copying `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`.** Return shape `{ interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }` so the loop (and logs) can distinguish outage ride-through from other interrupts. The `transient` flag is additive and internal-only.
4. **`executeIntegrationAssignment` gets the same branch (parity).** Same classifier, same interrupt+return shape. Cost is a few lines; leaving it out would keep "backend restart kills an integrate job's process" as a known hole. (Single-shot mode still ends the process either way — see Decision 6.)
5. **Idle loop: bounded retries with backoff on idempotent calls (survey q3), minimum sleep-and-continue.** `dispatchClaim` classifier-positive errors: retry up to N (recommended 3) with growing waits (recommended 1s→2s→4s, capped at `pollMs`), then keep waiting (back off one `pollMs` and re-poll) without consuming idle budget and without exiting — mirroring the existing 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches (lines 2980–2997). Join-time (`joinAndHeartbeat`) transient failures: add the same bounded retry at startup only if the Step 0 probe confirms join is a live crash path during outages; otherwise document as a follow-up, not scope creep.
6. **Fatal set unchanged: `STALE_EPOCH`, auth/credential failures, unknown errors.** `STALE_EPOCH` keeps propagating in all three catches (epoch fencing). Auth failures (401/credential rejection) exit loud — retrying them would spin forever on a revoked credential. 121|| Fatality boundary (GUIDE-04 §3) | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (new boundary tests) | Transient returns + interrupt-with-reason + loop polls on; stale-epoch rethrows |
122|| No-regression on unknown | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (`persistent-loop-probe` test) | Passes unmodified — unknown dispatch errors still throw |
123|| Focused client tests | `node --test runner/client.test.js` | All pass (classifier export does not disturb existing shapes) |
124|| Registration pin | `node --test tests/run-tests.test.mjs` (or via `npm test`) | Green with the new suite file listed |
125|| Full unit gate | `npm test` | Green (runner suite included via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) |
126|| Scope audit | `git diff --stat` + grep `isTransientBackendError` in `runner/` | Only the files listed in Step 5; db49 loop catch untouched |
127|| Manual repro | `/tmp` script from Step 0 re-run post-fix | Mid-assignment 502 → interrupt+return; dispatch 502s → backoff + re-poll, no exit |
128|| Prod confirm (needs permission) | E4 timestamp-join; journal crash-restart rate vs assignment success | Restart rate drops across backend windows; success holds |
129|
130|Highest-risk validation: the Step 4 daemon boundary tests — `runDispatchLoop` is poll-driven, so bound the loop deterministically with the existing `stubClient`/`loopConfig({ dispatchPollMs: 1, dispatchIdleLimit })` seams (never wall-clock sleeps); follow the existing `runDispatchLoop` tests' count-then-succeed stub pattern.
131|
132|## Risks
133|
134|- **Over-matching the classifier (q2 trade-off):** an over-broad network set could swallow an auth or fencing failure and spin instead of exiting loud. Mitigation: allowlist only `502/503/504` + observed socket shapes; explicit negative tests for 401/`STALE_EPOCH`/429/500; match on stable `code`/`statusCode`, not message substrings.
135|- **Under-matching on undici version drift:** fetch-failure text varies by Node version. Mitigation: Step 0 derives shapes on the repo's pinned Node; predicate prefers `cause.code`/absence-of-`statusCode` signals.
136|- **Poison-task flap:** after S4, a persistently-502ing backend call re-queues the task each attempt (runner survives, task flaps until the backend heals). Strictly better than a restart storm; consecutive-failure backoff is out of scope (see Non-goals).
137|- **Interrupt-during-outage is best-effort by necessity:** the ride-through interrupt itself may 502; the lease TTL is the backstop (same as every sibling branch). The one-line log preserves discoverability.
138|- **Missing source research:** GUIDE-04 §2/§3 shapes are reconstructed (see Evidence gap). Mitigation: shapes are re-derived from the observed client code in Step 0; reconcile with upstream docs if they surface.
139|
140|## Non-goals
141|
142|- Any change to the db49d6c6 loop-level catch (it stays exactly as-is) or to `interrupt` → `complete(failed)` routing for generic errors.
143|- Retrying non-idempotent calls (`complete`, `interrupt` stay single-attempt best-effort); retries apply only to idempotent idle calls (dispatch poll, and join/heartbeat only per Step 3's probe).
144|- Consecutive-failure backoff/circuit-breaking for flapping tasks; treating HTTP 500 as transient.
145|- `--no-verify`, worktree, hook, or systemd unit changes.
146|- Running the PROD-READ-ONLY E4 timestamp-join or journal analysis without the permission grant.
147|
148|## Open Questions
149|
150|1. **Survey confirmation:** `SURVEY.md` answers are empty — confirm the four adopted recommended options (q1 stay-alive+report, q2 transient-only survival, q3 bounded backoff retries, q4 one-line log). If q3's simpler "just wait and re-check" is preferred, Step 3 collapses to the sleep-and-continue minimum with no retry counter. (Default if unanswered: proceed as planned.)
151|2. **Single-shot mapping (Decision 6):** confirm transient-interrupted in `runSingleAssignment` should exit non-zero with the reason (recommended, preserves the CI contract) rather than exit 0. If 0 is required, Step 2 skips the mapping.
152|3. ** Retry budget (Decision 5):** confirm 3 attempts / 1s→2s→4s backoff for dispatch-poll retries, or name other bounds. Any reasonable bound fits the same code shape.
153|4. None other — all technical facts above were verified in-repo this session except the noted source-folder gap.
154|
155|## Work estimate / sequencing note
156|
157|Big/research pieces first per the stage brief: Step 0 (chain verification + exact error-shape derivation + upstream doc reconcile) and the Step 3 join-time probe are the riskiest and come before/around the small behavior edits. Steps 1–3 are small and mechanical once the classifier set is fixed. Total: 5 implementation steps + gates, all in `runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js`, `runner/daemon.test.js`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, plus a short `runner/README.md` note and the post-rollout confirm (permission-gated).

#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: run-tests.mjs
 * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven
 *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the
 *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), the Dependency
 *   Audit Gate, the Proof Hygiene branch, and the Binary Guard branch, in a
 *   single overlap window
 *   (the two unit suites
 *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one
 *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —
 *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on
 *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out
 *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches
 *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security
 *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).
 *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs
 *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit
 *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit
 *   suites. Fail-fast is ON by default (see resolveFailFast): when the fast
 *   phase fails, the gate writes its verdict (`verdict.json` plus one
 *   untrimmed `<branch-slug>.full.log` per failed branch) under
 *   `$KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS/ci-fast-gate-<timestamp>/`, prints the
 *   `KAINBAIN_FAST_GATE_RESULT` banner, and skips the serial canary phase
 *   with an explicit SKIP line — so the failure surfaces seconds after the
 *   fast phase instead of ~13 minutes later. Opt out with `--no-fail-fast`
 *   or `KAINBAIN_NO_FAIL_FAST=1` (canary still runs after a red fast phase,
 *   but the verdict still lands early). A green fast phase always runs
 *   canary (the #KB-0417 parity requirement); deploy.sh --prod passes
 *   `--no-canary` to its final-test-suite gate, so fail-fast changes
 *   nothing there. Failure Details tails stay bounded (120 lines by
 *   default, `KAINBAIN_FAILURE_TAIL_LINES` to tune) with a `Full log:`
 *   pointer at the untrimmed file; the verdict pointers are printed at the
 *   gate's head and tail so they survive the engine's head+tail excerpts.
 *   The Container Tests branch runs the static Dockerfile/compose assertions
 *   only; the minutes-long live image build/boot tests are opt-in via
 *   `KAINBAIN_CONTAINER_TESTS=live` (direct suite run, not the gate).
 *   The Canary Tests branch (serial Playwright suite on its own scratch
 *   stack, ~7 min) is IN the default gate so `npm test` and
 *   `deploy.sh --prod` run the exact same suites and regressions surface in
 *   the earliest automated stage, not at the merge/deploy gate (the
 *   #KB-0417 incident). Opt out with `--no-canary` or
 *   `KAINBAIN_SKIP_CANARY=1` for fast sanity cycles; `deploy.sh --prod`
 *   passes `--no-canary` to its `final-test-suite` gate and runs the canary
 *   suite as its own blocking `canary-e2e` gate, so nothing runs twice.
 *   Measured gate wall is ~60-70s without canary (the two unit suites alone
 *   are ~160s of CPU work) and ~366-420s with canary (the serial Playwright
 *   suite is minutes long), so CI stages running this gate need an explicit
 *   `timeout` override well above the 60s engine default
 *   (`config.ciTimeoutMs`) — this project's stage sets 1800s. While branches
 *   run the gate emits `▸ started <name>` lines and a `⏳ still running: …`
 *   tick every 30s (`KAINBAIN_GATE_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS`), so a slow branch
 *   never blanks the output (see scripts/lib/run-parallel.mjs).
 *   `run-tests.sh` is a thin shim over this file so `deploy.sh --prod` and
 *   older docs keep working.
 * @example `npm test` => thirteen PASS lines (twelve fast branches + Canary Tests), exit 0
 * @example `npm test -- --no-canary` => twelve PASS lines, exit 0
 ***/

#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: run-tests.mjs
 * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven
 *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the
 *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), the Dependency
 *   Audit Gate, the Proof Hygiene branch, and the Binary Guard branch, in a
 *   single overlap window
 *   (the two unit suites
 *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one
 *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —
 *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on
 *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out
 *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches
 *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security
 *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).
 *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs
 *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit
 *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit
 *   suites. Fail-fast is ON by default (see resolveFailFast): when the fast
 *   phase fails, the gate writes its verdict (`verdict.json` plus one
 *   untrimmed `<branch-slug>.full.log` per failed branch) under
 *   `$KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS/ci-fast-gate-<timestamp>/`, prints the
 *   `KAINBAIN_FAST_GATE_RESULT` banner, and skips the serial canary phase
 *   with an explicit SKIP line — so the failure surfaces seconds after the
 *   fast phase instead of ~13 minutes later. Opt out with `--no-fail-fast`
 *   or `KAINBAIN_NO_FAIL_FAST=1` (canary still runs after a red fast phase,
 *   but the verdict still lands early). A green fast phase always runs
 *   canary (the #KB-0417 parity requirement); deploy.sh --prod passes
 *   `--no-canary` to its final-test-suite gate, so fail-fast changes
 *   nothing there. Failure Details tails stay bounded (120 lines by
 *   default, `KAINBAIN_FAILURE_TAIL_LINES` to tune) with a `Full log:`
 *   pointer at the untrimmed file; the verdict pointers are printed at the
 *   gate's head and tail so they survive the engine's head+tail excerpts.
 *   The Container Tests branch runs the static Dockerfile/compose assertions
 *   only; the minutes-long live image build/boot tests are opt-in via
 *   `KAINBAIN_CONTAINER_TESTS=live` (direct suite run, not the gate).
 *   The Canary Tests branch (serial Playwright suite on its own scratch
 *   stack, ~7 min) is IN the default gate so `npm test` and
 *   `deploy.sh --prod` run the exact same suites and regressions surface in
 *   the earliest automated stage, not at the merge/deploy gate (the

Read text file `docs/tasks/78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — In-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4)
2|
3|Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`
4|Source problem: any in-try backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and rethrows → process exit → systemd restart, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run (501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502s since 11-19 on server2-alpha; proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).
5|Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1, q1–q4; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).
6|
7|## Goal
8|
9|1. Transient backend errors (fetch-failed network errors, HTTP 502/503/504) raised during an assignment make `executeAssignment` send an interrupt WITH a reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing — the same report-and-return precedent as the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and deterministic-gitFailure branches.
10|2. The idle loop stops crash-cycling on backend outages: bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (dispatch poll; heartbeat already warn-continues), or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit.
11|3. The non-fatal set is enumerated explicitly; `STALE_EPOCH`, auth failures, and genuinely unknown errors stay fatal. No inverted catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.
12|4. Regression tests in `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (+ daemon fatality-boundary tests) prove the transient/fatal boundary, registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.
13|
14|## Success Criteria
15|
16|- A 502/503/504 or dropped-socket failure from any backend call inside `executeAssignment` produces a best-effort `interrupt` carrying a reason, a one-line log naming the cause, and a return (no throw) — the dispatch loop keeps polling and the process stays alive.
17|- A dispatch-poll (`dispatchClaim`) transient failure backs off and re-polls without consuming idle budget and without exiting; restart counters stop incrementing across a backend restart window.
18|- `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (epoch fencing intact), auth/credential failures still exit loud, and unknown errors still throw — proven by boundary tests asserting `rethrown === false` for transient and `rethrown === true` for stale-epoch.
19|- `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js runner/daemon.test.js runner/client.test.js` passes, the repo unit gate (`npm test` via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes, and the new suite file is registered (the `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pin fails the gate if it is not).
20|- Post-rollout (needs PROD-READ-ONLY permission): crash-restart rate in the runner journal drops across backend restart windows while assignment success holds; E4 timestamp-join confirmed on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`.
21|
22|## Survey decisions (factored in)
23|
24|Local `SURVEY.md` Round 1 is unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions). The stage brief also cites the source-task survey q5 ("survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal") — that maps to local q2 and is adopted the same way.
25|
26|| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
27||---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
28|| q1 | Mid-task connection drop: what should the worker do? | Stay alive, report what happened, keep checking for work | Interrupt-with-reason + return; never rethrow for the transient set. |
29|| q2 (= source q5) | Which problems to survive vs still stop for? | Only survive short connection problems (network errors, 502/503/504); still stop for login problems, outdated orders, anything unknown | Explicit non-fatal enumeration (`isTransientBackendError`); `STALE_EPOCH`/auth/unknown stay fatal. |
30|| q3 | Idle poll/heartbeat outage: what to do? | Retry a few times with growing waits, then keep waiting without restarting | Bounded retries with backoff on idempotent idle calls; minimum acceptable fallback is sleep-and-continue. |
31|| q4 (optional) | Log visibility for ride-through? | A clear one-line note naming the cause, then keep going | One `warn`/`error` line with cause + task/project IDs per ride-through; no per-retry spam (retry attempts at debug/quiet). |
32|
33|## Approach
34|
35|Follow "make the change easy, then make the change", and build on the db49d6c6 containment — do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure:
36|
37|1. **Easy first:** extract one shared `isTransientBackendError(err)` classifier (single home for the explicit non-fatal set) plus shared test fixtures (502-shape stub, dropped-socket stub), with zero behavior change. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
38|2. **Then the change:** add one narrow branch in the `executeAssignment` catch using the classifier (interrupt-with-reason + return), mirroring the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape; same one-branch treatment for the `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (parity, decided in Key Decision 4).
39|3. **Then the idle loop:** transient-aware handling in the `dispatchClaim` catch (backoff + re-poll, no idle-budget consumption); verify the heartbeat timer path already tolerates outages (it warns-and-continues today) and add bounded join-time retries only if the Step 0 probe shows join is a live crash path.
40|4. **Then proof:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + daemon boundary tests, registration in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, red→green runs, full gates, rollout/confirm plan.
41|
42|No new dependencies, no new config flags (backoff constants are module-local), no schema/wire changes (the interrupt `reason` field already exists).
43|
44|## Evidence (what the research established)
45|
46|Verified in-repo this session (line numbers are the current checkout — re-verify at implementation time):
47|
48|- **In-assignment catch:** `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js` ~2296–2453) special-cases `STALE_EPOCH` (rethrow, line 2298), `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (interrupt-with-reason + return, lines 2299–2315), deterministic gitFailure (report + return, lines 2316–2376), `failedOutcome` (failed completion, lines 2377–2428), then the generic path: flush, best-effort interrupt with reason, **`throw err`** (lines 2441–2452). The S4 branch slots in just before the generic path, copying the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape.
49|- **db49d6c6 containment already landed (build on it):** `runDispatchLoop` wraps `executeAssignment` in try/catch (~3097–3153): `STALE_EPOCH` rethrows, anything else is logged and contained. So in dispatch mode a rethrow no longer exits — but the stage brief's crash path is still live in three places: (a) `dispatchClaim` unknown errors `throw err` at line 3018 → loop exits → systemd restart (this is the 366→367 crash-cycling); (b) `runSingleAssignment` has no loop, so any rethrow exits non-zero; (c) `joinAndHeartbeat` failures before the loop starts exit the process. S4 must target exactly these, not rework the db49 catch.
50|- **Client error shapes** (`runner/client.js` `call`, lines 17–40): non-2xx throws `Error` with `statusCode = res.status` and `code = data?.code ?? null` — so a 502 arrives as `{ statusCode: 502, code }`. A dropped socket / refused connection rejects `fetchImpl` itself (raw `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET` causes) with no `statusCode`. The classifier must cover both shapes.
51|- **Heartbeat already tolerates outages:** the periodic timer (`deliverSteers(...).catch(warn)`, lines 1241–1245) and claim renewal (`claimHeartbeat(...).then(warn)`, lines 796–808) both warn-and-continue; heartbeat failures ride the lease TTL. The idle-loop crash-cycling is the dispatch-poll path, not the heartbeat path.
52|- **Integration parity site:** `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (~2655–2697) ends in the same interrupt + `throw err` (lines 2687–2696).
53|- **Fatality contract pinned by an existing test:** `runner/daemon.test.js` "never idles out with dispatchIdleLimit 0" throws a generic `persistent-loop-probe` error from `dispatchClaim` and asserts the loop rejects — unknown dispatch errors MUST keep throwing after S4 (consistent with q2). S4's dispatch branch must only catch the classifier-positive set.
54|- **Test seams to reuse:** `stubClient` / `fakeHarness` / `localRepo` / `loopConfig` helpers and the `waitFor` polling helper in `runner/daemon.test.js`; `stubFetch` + `ok`/`fail` helpers in `runner/client.test.js`.
55|- **Test registration:** `scripts/run-tests.mjs` "Unit Tests (runner)" (~lines 460–491) names every `runner/*.test.js` explicitly, and `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every suite file on disk is registered — a new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` must be added to that list or the gate fails.
56|- **Evidence gap (does not block):** the cited source-research folder `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/` (`RESPONSE.md` S4, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 4, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q5) is absent from this checkout (verified: no such folder; repo-wide search for `backend-unreachable|WIDE_NET|Backend 502` finds nothing). The GUIDE-04 §2/§3 test shapes are therefore reconstructed from the stage brief plus the in-repo client shapes above; Step 0 re-derives the exact 502/dropped-socket fixtures from `runner/client.js` and Node fetch behavior rather than trusting the brief's prose. If the folder exists upstream, pull it in Step 0 and reconcile (shapes should match; any conflict is resolved in favor of the observed client behavior).
57|
58|## Key Decisions
59|
60|1. **Explicit non-fatal enumeration, never an inverted catch-all (survey q2).** One `isTransientBackendError(err)` predicate owns the set: `statusCode ∈ {502, 503, 504}` OR a network-layer failure (fetch rejection: `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`/`EAI_AGAIN`/socket-hangup causes — exact list fixed in Step 0 from observed shapes). Everything else falls through to today's generic path. New failure modes stay loud by construction.
61|2. **Classifier lives next to the client, used by the daemon.** Recommended: export from `runner/client.js` (it defines the error shapes) and import in `runner/daemon.js`. Rejected: duplicating status checks at each catch site (drifts), or putting it in `shared/` (runner-only concern; no backend/wire change).
62|3. **In-assignment branch = interrupt-with-reason + return, copying `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`.** Return shape `{ interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }` so the loop (and logs) can distinguish outage ride-through from other interrupts. The `transient` flag is additive and internal-only.
63|4. **`executeIntegrationAssignment` gets the same branch (parity).** Same classifier, same interrupt+return shape. Cost is a few lines; leaving it out would keep "backend restart kills an integrate job's process" as a known hole. (Single-shot mode still ends the process either way — see Decision 6.)
64|5. **Idle loop: bounded retries with backoff on idempotent calls (survey q3), minimum sleep-and-continue.** `dispatchClaim` classifier-positive errors: retry up to N (recommended 3) with growing waits (recommended 1s→2s→4s, capped at `pollMs`), then keep waiting (back off one `pollMs` and re-poll) without consuming idle budget and without exiting — mirroring the existing 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches (lines 2980–2997). meta.output:
# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment

Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).

## Goal

1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.

## Success Criteria

- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.

## Survey decisions (factored in)

`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):

| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |

## Approach

Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":

1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.

No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.

## Evidence (what the research established)

- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.
- **Crash path:** `executeAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2243–2333) catches generic errors, best-effort `client.interrupt`s, then **rethrows** (line 2332). `runDispatchLoop` awaits `executeAssignment` (line 2928) with **no `try/catch`**, and the loop body has only `try/finally` — so the throw escapes `runLoop` → `main()` (`runner/main.js`) rejects → process exits 1 → systemd restarts → the interrupted task re-queues and the same poisoned worktree is reclaimed → observed 10,776-restart loop.  *   `pretty-proof.png` whose first byte had been rewritten to the UTF-8
 *   replacement character by a text-oriented edit tool — magic `ef bf bd`
 *   instead of PNG `89 50 4e 47`, `file` reporting `data` — plus a dead
 *   scratch file `rt.mjs` committed at the repo root).
 *   Two rule families, one script, one failure format:
 *   (1) magic-byte validation for proof images (everything image-typed under
 *   `docs/tasks/`, plus `*-proof.*` / `screenshot*` names anywhere under

 *   scripts, `*.log`/`*.tmp`, loose root images, `t<digits>.*` ad-hoc notes)
 *   unless the exact path is allowlisted in
 *   `scripts/allowlists/repo-root-files.json`.
 *   Reads actual bytes from disk (worktree + tracked set), so corruption
 *   introduced before staging is still caught. Unknown extensions and files
 *   that vanish mid-scan are skipped, never failed: this is a corruption
 *   detector, not file-type police — but an UNREADABLE proof file fails, so
 *   an unverifiable file can never pass. Symlinks are followed (link path,
 *   target bytes); broken links are skipped. Dependency-free (Node stdlib
 *   only). An invocation that cannot run (bad flag, stray argument, missing
 *   `--root` directory) exits 2 — never a false PASS.
 *   Pre-existing violations owned by other tasks (corrupt on origin/main
 *   with no valid source to restore) are recorded in
 *   `scripts/baselines/proof-hygiene-known-violations.json` — the repo's
 *   established baseline pattern (cf. jsdoc-example-missing.json) — so the
 *   gate stays green while still failing on any NEW violation. `--strict`
 *   fails on baselined entries too (acceptance rehearsal, detector proof).
 *   A passing run names baseline entries that matched nothing, so healed
 *   or deleted files get pruned instead of rotting the baseline.
 * @example node scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs (exit 0 on a clean tree)
 * @example node scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs --root /tmp/fixture-tree
 * @example node scripts/check-proof-and-hygiene.mjs --strict
 ***/

+ *   502/503/504 (the backend or its proxy is restarting) plus
+ *   network-layer fetch rejections where the backend never answered

+ *   matched on stable `code`/`cause.code` signals, never message text).

+// e.g. a destroyed socket surfaces as UND_ERR_SOCKET on Node 20/22/24).

+	"ENOTFOUND",
+	"EPIPE",
+	"EHOSTUNREACH",
